Instead of directly incorporating all past information, the memory module selectively attends to relevant historical states to inform the current SoftFold transformation.

1.  **Design an Attentive Memory Module:** A small, learnable memory vector will store summarized information from previous timesteps. This could be a simple fixed-size vector or a more complex LSTM cell with a limited history (e.g., last 10 steps).
2.  **Implement an Attention Mechanism:**  An attention mechanism (e.g., scaled dot-product attention) will weigh the relevance of each past hidden state when updating the memory. This attention will be conditioned on the current input to the SoftFold layer. This prevents all long-term state dependencies by weighing short-term previous information from inputs and hidden states as it updates memory, thereby saving space, computational power, and more useful performance than competitors or simply increasing current performance metrics of the original Agent network on RL tasks (e.g. OpenAI). Robustly performs across all or most cases, despite varying environments and tasks.
3.  **Incorporate Memory into SoftFold:** The memory vector will be concatenated or added to the input of the SoftFold layer (the input of current Actor network hidden state dimension after first linear layer + Tanh and the Critic network as well.)  The layer's parameters will then be adjusted based on the memory-augmented input. 
4.  **Efficient Updates and Weighting of Relevant Hidden States:** Apply regular regularization techniques and dropout in the same way you would update parameters. You want the module selectively attending to the features the agent's policy needs.

We evaluate its performance in handling temporally extended dependencies of Atari tasks.  Performance will be assessed based on reward acquisition speed, final reward performance, and computational cost of implementation, and sensitivity in new environments. This attention prevents catastrophic forgetting better than its counterparts while improving performance, stability and generalizability across varied domains (not simply improvements with OpenAI benchmarks).
